_about: Road types. Lengths and widths are metres, speeds km/h, capacity vehicles per hour per lane, slopes rise over run. Prices are whole dollars in their source year; `escalation` brings them to 2026. A type's place in `types` is its id in saves, so append new types and never reorder. `demolitionCostPerMetre` is what bulldozing a metre costs, times the bridge multiplier on a bridge. A type's `bridge` sets the longest bridge it can make, in metres, and how many times its price per metre a bridge costs. Speeds, capacities, widths and limits are starting values to tune. Issue 47 relaxed the grades and curve radii of the buildable types and raised every bridge limit to the longest bridge over water.

escalation.source: Eno Center for Transportation, highway construction cost index: up about 59 percent from mid 2021 to the end of 2025. 1.59 over 4.5 years is 1.1085 a year.

build._about: How the sim checks a road before it builds one. Lengths are metres, angles degrees. `bridgeClearance` is how far a bridge deck sits above the water. `upgradeCredit` is the share of the old road's build cost taken off an upgrade's price, because the roadbed is reused; a placeholder with no source. `undoSteps` is how many road changes each player can take back. `gridMaxStreets` is the most streets one `BuildRoadGrid` lays, counting each grid line as one street before water or slopes cut it; it keeps the step that applies a grid inside the tick budget. `gridMinBlockShare` is the smallest share of the asked-for block size the last block along a side may have before it joins its neighbour. Starting values to tune.

levels._about: Heights of a segment's levels, in metres above the ground under it: a tunnel below, two elevated levels above. A bridge is not here: its deck height comes from the water (`build.bridgeClearance`). `clearance` is the least height, road surface to road surface, at which two roads cross without a junction; closer than that but not level, the road is refused. It is the 16 ft (4.9 m) vertical clearance FHWA sets for Interstates plus 1.6 m of deck structure, which is a placeholder. The heights are placeholders chosen so each level clears the one below it.
levels.source: FHWA, Interstate design standards: 16 ft vertical clearance on rural Interstates and one urban routing, from the 2016 revision of the controlling criteria. The 1.6 m deck depth is a placeholder.

buildCostPerMetre.source: Placeholder. Half the Phoenix 4-lane arterial figure, scaled by lane count. No usable source for a local street was found.
buildCostPerMetre.note: FDOT's Cost Per Mile Models list a new 2-lane undivided urban arterial (U01) at about $9.1M per mile, but that is an arterial with bike lanes and drainage, its price year could not be confirmed, and it would make a street cost more than an avenue.

upkeepPerMetrePerYear.source: Placeholder. One percent of the build cost a year, until M4 prices upkeep.

demolitionCostPerMetre.source: Placeholder. $30 per square metre of pavement removed, times the 10 m width, until M4 prices demolition.

bridge.maxLengthSource: The longest continuous bridge over water, the Lake Pontchartrain Causeway in Louisiana, is 38.4 km (Guinness World Records, 2011). Longer than the 12 km map, so in practice any water a road can reach it can bridge (issue 47).
bridge.source: Arkansas DOT, Bridge Cost 2023: $339.54 per square foot of deck ($3,655 per square metre) for off-NHS bridges let in the 2023 federal fiscal year. Deck width is the road width plus 2 m of barriers; the multiplier is that cost per metre over the road's own price per metre.
bridge.note: 12 m of deck is $43,860 a metre, over the street's $1,400. The street price is a placeholder, so this is too.
